In [[algebraic geometry]], given a [[smooth curve|smooth]] [[projective curve]] ''X'' over a [[finite field]] <math>\mathbf{F}_q</math> and a smooth [[affine group scheme|affine]] [[group scheme]] ''G'' over it, the '''moduli stack of principal bundles''' over ''X'', denoted by <math>\operatorname{Bun}_G(X)</math>, is an [[algebraic stack]] given by:<ref>{{citation |url=http://www.math.harvard.edu/~lurie/283notes/Lecture2-FunctionFields.pdf|title=Tamagawa Numbers in the Function Field Case (Lecture 2)|first=Jacob|last=Lurie|date=April 3, 2013 |access-date=2014-01-30 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130411033546/http://www.math.harvard.edu/~lurie/283notes/Lecture2-FunctionFields.pdf |archive-date=2013-04-11 |url-status=dead }}</ref> for any <math>\mathbf{F}_q</math>-algebra ''R'',
:<math>\operatorname{Bun}_G(X)(R)= </math> the category of [[torsor|principal ''G''-bundles]] over the relative curve <math>X \times_{\mathbf{F}_q} \operatorname{Spec}R</math>.
In particular, the category of <math>\mathbf{F}_q</math>-points of <math>\operatorname{Bun}_G(X)</math>, that is, <math>\operatorname{Bun}_G(X)(\mathbf{F}_q)</math>, is the category of ''G''-bundles over ''X''.

Similarly, <math>\operatorname{Bun}_G(X)</math> can also be defined when the curve ''X'' is over the field of complex numbers. Roughly, in the complex case, one can define <math>\operatorname{Bun}_G(X)</math> as the [[quotient stack]] of the space of holomorphic connections on ''X'' by the [[gauge group (mathematics)|gauge group]]. Replacing the quotient stack (which is not a topological space) by a [[homotopy quotient]] (which is a topological space) gives the [[homotopy type]] of <math>\operatorname{Bun}_G(X)</math>.

In the finite field case, it is not common to define the homotopy type of <math>\operatorname{Bun}_G(X)</math>. But one can still define a ([[smooth topology|smooth]]) [[cohomology]] and [[Homology (mathematics)|homology]] of <math>\operatorname{Bun}_G(X)</math>.

== Basic properties ==
It is known that <math>\operatorname{Bun}_G(X)</math> is a [[smooth stack]] of dimension <math>(g(X) - 1) \dim G</math> where <math>g(X)</math> is the genus of ''X''. It is not of finite type but locally of finite type; one thus usually uses a stratification by open substacks of finite type (cf. the [[Harder–Narasimhan stratification]]), also for parahoric G over curve X see <ref>{{harvnb|Heinloth|2010|loc=Proposition 2.1.2}}</ref> and for G only a flat group scheme of finite type over X see.<ref>{{citation
 | last1 = Arasteh Rad | first1 = E.
 | last2 = Hartl | first2 = Urs
 | arxiv = 1302.6351
 | doi = 10.1093/imrn/rnz223
 | issue = 21
 | journal = International Mathematics Research Notices
 | mr = 4338216
 | pages = 16121–16192
 | title = Uniformizing the moduli stacks of global G-shtukas
 | year = 2021}}; see Theorem 2.5</ref>  

If ''G'' is a split reductive group, then the set of connected components <math>\pi_0(\operatorname{Bun}_G(X))</math> is in a natural bijection with the fundamental group <math>\pi_1(G)</math>.<ref>{{harvnb|Heinloth|2010|loc=Proposition 2.1.2}}</ref>
<!--
Put <math>S = \operatorname{Spec} k</math>. Denoting by ''BG'' the [[classifying stack]] of ''G'' and by <math>\pi: X \to S</math> the structure map, the direct image <math>\pi_* BG</math> is denoted by <math>\operatorname{Bun}_G(X)</math>. Explicitly, <math>\operatorname{Bun}_G</math> is a product of <math>BG_x</math> running over <math>x \in X</math>.

The following facts appear in  Beilinson–Drinfeld's "quantization of hitchin's integrable system and hecke eigensheaves". Let ''X'' be a smooth projective curve of genus g > 1. Then <math>\operatorname{Bun}_G = \operatorname{Bun}_G(X)</math> is a smooth algebraic stack of pure dimension <math>(g-1) \operatorname{dim} G</math>. The canonical line bundle on <math>\operatorname{Bun}_G</math> is the determinant of the [[cotangent complex]] of <math>\operatorname{Bun}_G</math>.

Let <math>p: T^* \operatorname{Bun}_G \to \operatorname{Hitch}(X)</math> be the [[Hitchin fibration]]. Then <math>p^{-1}(0)</math> is called the [[global nilpotent cone]]. Its dimension is the same as that of <math>\operatorname{Hitch}(X)</math> (a theorem of Faltings and Ginzburg); in fact, it is [[Lagrangian submanifold|lagrangian]].
-->

== Behrend's trace formula ==
{{see also|Weil conjecture on Tamagawa numbers|Behrend's formula}}
This is a (conjectural) version of the [[Lefschetz trace formula]] for <math>\operatorname{Bun}_G(X)</math> when ''X'' is over a finite field, introduced by [[Kai Behrend|Behrend]] in 1993.<ref>{{citation|url=http://www.math.ubc.ca/~behrend/thesis.pdf|title=The Lefschetz Trace Formula for the Moduli Stack of Principal Bundles|first=Kai A.|last=Behrend|type=PhD thesis|publisher=University of California, Berkeley|year=1991}}</ref> It states:<ref>{{harvnb|Gaitsgory|Lurie|2019|loc=Chapter 5: The Trace Formula for Bun<sub>G</sub>(X), p. 260}}</ref> if ''G'' is a [[smooth scheme|smooth]] affine [[group scheme]] with semisimple connected [[generic fiber]], then
:<math>\# \operatorname{Bun}_G(X)(\mathbf{F}_q) = q^{\dim \operatorname{Bun}_G(X)} \operatorname{tr} (\phi^{-1}|H^*(\operatorname{Bun}_G(X); \mathbb{Z}_l))</math>
where (see also [[Behrend's trace formula]] for the details)
*''l'' is a prime number that is not ''p'' and the ring <math>\mathbb{Z}_l</math> of [[l-adic integers]] is viewed as a subring of <math>\mathbb{C}</math>.
*<math>\phi</math> is the [[geometric Frobenius]].
*<math>\# \operatorname{Bun}_G(X)(\mathbf{F}_q) = \sum_P {1 \over \# \operatorname{Aut}(P)}</math>, the sum running over all isomorphism classes of [[torsor (algebraic geometry)|G-bundles]] on ''X'' and convergent.
*<math>\operatorname{tr}(\phi^{-1}|V_*) = \sum_{i = 0}^\infty (-1)^i \operatorname{tr}(\phi^{-1}|V_i)</math> for a [[graded vector space]] <math>V_*</math>, provided the [[series (mathematics)|series]] on the right absolutely converges.
''A priori,'' neither left nor right side in the formula converges. Thus, the formula states that the two sides converge to finite numbers and that those numbers coincide.
<!--
The [[Siegel mass formula]] computes the right-hand side.

Mention [[Tamagawa number]].
-->
